Transaction boundary used by the request middleware.

Handlers originally committed by hand, and a forgotten commit silently
discarded writes when the pooled connection was recycled. The middleware
now opens one scope per request and commits when the handler returns
normally. Any exception, including ones the handler later converts to an
error response, triggers a rollback first. Savepoints are intentionally
unsupported, so partial failures inside a handler must be handled before
the scope exits.

The first protocol revision used a 2-byte length, which capped messages at 64 KiB and

type, and a 4-byte big-endian length, in that order. The agent still accepts version 1

Length-prefixed framing with a CRC32 trailer.

Every frame ends with a 4-byte CRC32 of the payload only; the length prefix is not
covered. A corrupted length therefore surfaces as a checksum failure on whatever bytes
happen to follow, not as a distinct error. After a ChecksumError the stream position is
undefined, so callers should close the connection instead of trying to resynchronize.

Graceful shutdown helpers for the ingest pipeline.

These were added after a deploy left half-written batch files on disk:
the old code cancelled tasks and exited without waiting for them to
unwind. Each stage is now shielded while it commits its batch, so a
cancellation request is delivered only after the commit finishes. The
scheduler in the orchestrator calls shutdown() on SIGTERM and expects

Transaction boundary used by the request middleware.

Handlers originally committed by hand, and a forgotten commit silently
discarded writes when the pooled connection was recycled. The middleware
now opens one scope per request and commits when the handler returns
normally. Any exception, including ones the handler later converts to an
error response, triggers a rollback first. Savepoints are intentionally
unsupported, so partial failures inside a handler must be handled before
the scope exits.

Wire framing shared by the agent and the CLI client.

The first protocol revision used a 2-byte length, which capped messages at 64 KiB and
broke once file listings grew past that. Frames now carry a 1-byte version, a 1-byte
type, and a 4-byte big-endian length, in that order. The agent still accepts version 1
frames from older clients, so the version byte must stay first in the header.
Payloads above MAX_PAYLOAD are rejected on both the write and read paths.

Length-prefixed framing with a CRC32 trailer.

Every frame ends with a 4-byte CRC32 of the payload only; the length prefix is not
covered. A corrupted length therefore surfaces as a checksum failure on whatever bytes

Workers take paths from a shared queue and append results under a lock.

on the condition and wakes on every increment, so it redraws once per

read from CSV exports before they are loaded into the warehouse.

Email canonicalization used when joining contact records across sources.

different forms of the same address, which produced duplicate customers. To
fix this, the join key strips "+tag" suffixes from the local part and
removes dots for gmail.com addresses only. The canonical form is meant for
matching and must never be written back as the contact's display address.
The domain is always lowercased via an IDNA-aware step in the loader.

Replacement for the system clock injected into the deadline checker.

The checker used to call datetime.now() directly, which made overdue tests
depend on wall time and fail around midnight. It now takes a clock object,
and this stub stores a list of timestamps that are handed out one per call
to now(). Running out of values raises IndexError on purpose, so a test
that reads the clock more often than expected fails loudly.

Remove a per-request scratch directory after the response is sent.

Request handlers used to rely on the framework's teardown hook, but it does
not run when a client disconnects mid-stream, which left scratch trees
piling up. Handlers now call this from a finally block. The path must be
inside root; anything else raises ValueError so a bad request id can never
point the cleanup at an unrelated directory.

Render rows into a temporary file and return an open handle positioned at the start.

The file is created with delete=True, so it disappears as soon as the caller
closes the handle. Callers must not reopen it by name: on Windows that fails
while the handle is open. Intended to be passed straight to the response streamer.
Replace secret query parameter values in a URL with asterisks.

Mask secret values in parsed JSON before it reaches the audit log.

Walks dicts and lists recursively instead of regex-scrubbing the raw text,
which an earlier version did and which missed values containing escaped
quotes. Returns a new structure; the input is left untouched.

Regression: peeking at the first record to read the schema used to
drop it from the output, because next() advanced the shared iterator.
The helper now chains the peeked record back in front of the remainder,
so downstream stages receive the complete stream in original order.

# The registry's rate-limit window outlasts our 1/2/4 second schedule, and a fixed
# schedule once got CI tokens throttled, so a 429 carrying Retry-After sleeps for
# that many seconds instead. Only the integer form is handled; an HTTP-date value
# raises ValueError here and ends the retries.

Graceful shutdown helpers for the ingest pipeline.

These were added after a deploy left half-written batch files on disk:
the old code cancelled tasks and exited without waiting for them to
unwind. Each stage is now shielded while it commits its batch, so a
cancellation request is delivered only after the commit finishes. The
scheduler in the orchestrator calls shutdown() on SIGTERM and expects
it to return once every stage has stopped.

Transaction boundary used by the request middleware.

Handlers originally committed by hand, and a forgotten commit silently
discarded writes when the pooled connection was recycled. The middleware
now opens one scope per request and commits when the handler returns
normally. Any exception, including ones the handler later converts to an
error response, triggers a rollback first. Savepoints are intentionally
unsupported, so partial failures inside a handler must be handled before
the scope exits.

Transaction boundary used by the request middleware.

Handlers originally committed by hand, and a forgotten commit silently
discarded writes when the pooled connection was recycled. The middleware
now opens one scope per request and commits when the handler returns
normally. Any exception, including ones the handler later converts to an
error response, triggers a rollback first. Savepoints are intentionally
unsupported, so partial failures inside a handler must be handled before
the scope exits.

reports as several modify events within a few milliseconds. Earlier versions
deduplicated by path alone and lost genuine later edits, so two events count as
duplicates only when the path and kind match and their timestamps are within
window seconds of the last kept event. Input must be sorted by timestamp;
unsorted input can keep events that should have been merged.

Replacement for the system clock injected into the deadline checker.

The checker used to call datetime.now() directly, which made overdue tests
depend on wall time and fail around midnight. It now takes a clock object,
and this stub stores a list of timestamps that are handed out one per call
to now(). Running out of values raises IndexError on purpose, so a test
that reads the clock more often than expected fails loudly.

Remove a per-request scratch directory after the response is sent.

Request handlers used to rely on the framework's teardown hook, but it does
not run when a client disconnects mid-stream, which left scratch trees
piling up. Handlers now call this from a finally block. The path must be
inside root; anything else raises ValueError so a bad request id can never
point the cleanup at an unrelated directory.

Graceful shutdown helpers for the ingest pipeline.

These were added after a deploy left half-written batch files on disk:
the old code cancelled tasks and exited without waiting for them to
unwind. Each stage is now shielded while it commits its batch, so a
cancellation request is delivered only after the commit finishes. The
scheduler in the orchestrator calls shutdown() on SIGTERM and expects
it to return once every stage has stopped.

route receives a rejection type for what is really a fault. Recording it

Webhook delivery layer.

This module exists because the product team decided customer-facing
webhooks should be delivered out of the main request path so a slow
customer endpoint can never slow down our own API. That decision also
drove the choice of a separate queue rather than a thread pool: a thread
pool shares memory with the request workers and a stuck customer server
could exhaust it, whereas a queue isolates the blast radius entirely. We
also considered and rejected server-sent events for the same isolation
reason.

Figures out whether a given logging call would actually render stack
frames if it ran.

The presence of exc_info isn't the whole question: the logging module
treats a falsy exc_info as absent, so exception(..., exc_info=None) prints
no traceback even though the keyword is there, while a bare exception(...)
does print one because the method defaults exc_info to True. We walk the
AST node, look at its keywords, and decide based on that.
